name: hello
description: The example plugin: greets, sends a message to a thread through the host, keeps a word in the Keychain, follows the thread list, marks threads with a notification, gives new threads CF_HELLO=1, runs a Claude thread and a terminal of its own, ticks for subscribed threads, and posts notifications.

commands.name: send
commands.title: Send Hello to Thread
commands.description: Send a message to a thread through Code Foundry (thread.send).

args.name: thread
args.description: The thread (default: the active one, or --context-thread)

commands.name: remember
commands.title: Remember a Word
commands.description: Keep a word in the Keychain, in the plugin's own namespace.

commands.name: forget
commands.title: Forget the Word
commands.description: Remove the remembered word from the Keychain.

commands.name: unpin
commands.title: Unpin Hello
commands.description: Withdraw the pinned surface from a thread (the demo's Pin button adds it).

commands.name: mark
commands.title: Mark Thread
commands.description: Post (or with level none withdraw) a notification about a thread, one per thread: marking it again updates the card.

args.name: reason
args.description: The notification's title: one short line

args.name: thread
args.description: The thread (default: the active one, or --context-thread)

commands.name: read-shell
commands.title: Read the Clock Terminal
commands.description: Print the whole output of the clock terminal (the demo's Shell tab): its scrollback and its screen. Starts the clock when it is not running.

commands.name: events
commands.title: Count Thread Events
commands.description: Say how many thread list events the plugin received since it started.

commands.name: fire-tick
commands.title: Fire Tick Now
commands.description: Fire the tick wake source now: wake the threads subscribed to it.

args.name: every
args.description: Only the subscriptions with this every (default: each one armed)

args.name: time-sensitive
args.description: Make its notification time-sensitive: raised even when a thread gets the wake

commands.name: notify
commands.title: Post a Build Notification
commands.description: Post a notification about a failed build on a thread; its Open run button shows the run in the demo. With --withdraw, withdraw it.

args.name: thread
args.description: The thread (default: the active one, or --context-thread)

args.name: time-sensitive
args.description: Time-sensitive: first in the bell, in the Dock badge

commands.name: open-run
commands.title: Open a Run in the Demo
commands.description: Show a run in the demo's Runs tab beside a thread (the build notification's button).

args.name: thread
args.description: The thread (default: the active one, or --context-thread)

wakes.name: tick
wakes.title: Tick
wakes.description: Fires every <every> while a thread is subscribed (once without --repeat); the payload has the tick count. A demo of wake sources.
